title: Cache Thermostat: automated prefix TTL calibration and key minimization
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Inconsistent prefix TTLs and overgranular cache keys cause unpredictable token costs across workloads. Goal: Build an automated controller (the "Cache Thermostat") that recommends and safely applies per-prefix TTLs while suggesting a simplified key surface to reduce cardinality and improve hit rates. The system must produce conservative change suggestions, simulate expected cost/latency impact, and provide an automated rollback path if observed metrics deviate from predictions.
success_metrics: 1) Reduce per-request token cost by 8% on median workloads after rollout; 2) Maintain 95th latency within 5% of baseline; 3) No more than 0.5% of prefixes experience >25% degradation in hit rate post-apply; 4) Automated rollback engaged <3% of staged rollouts.
technical_approach: 1) Offline modeling: use sampled request traces to estimate per-prefix hit elasticity against TTL changes; 2) Synthesize compact key templates by greedy clustering of high-cardinality suffixes and preserve semantic segments; 3) Build a conservative TTL candidate generator that enumerates geometric TTL ladders and scores expected token-savings vs risk; 4) A staged apply harness: dry-run -> shadow -> canary -> gradual ramp with hyperparameters controlled by a safety controller (min-sample, min-qps, rollback thresholds).
data_and_simulation: We built a synthetic replay harness using 14 days of anonymized request traces from three representative customers. Simulation captures batching dynamics, prefix coalescing, and KV cache eviction behavior. Preliminary sims show a 6–12% token-cost reduction on the sample sets for aggressive TTL ladders, but with increased tail latency for some rare prefixes. We added a hit-rate confidence estimator (Beta posterior) per prefix to quantify uncertainty and to gate application for low-sample prefixes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Proposal review and safety parameter defaults (current). Phase 1 (dry-run): produce recommendations and compare simulated vs observed metrics for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (shadow): apply policies in shadow to live traffic but do not influence serving decisions; collect real delta signals for 72 hours. Phase 3 (canary): apply to 1% QPS with automated rollback thresholds (hit-rate drop >20% OR cost increase >5% sustained for 15 minutes). Phase 4: ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by monitoring guardrails.
rollback_plan: Rollback is automated and hierarchical: immediate local rollback for canary nodes when guard thresholds breach; global rollback via orchestration if multiple canaries signal failures. Use staging checkpoints and idempotent apply/unapply operations. Keep previous TTL map in git-backed config with migration tags and a fast path to rehydrate previous cache state where possible. Post-rollback, run root-cause analysis with replay of trace slice.
open_questions: 1) What default confidence threshold should gate low-volume prefixes? 2) Should key minimization be allowed to coalesce user-specific segments for any customer without opt-in? 3) How long should shadow phase run for enterprise customers with seasonal traffic?
decisions_made: 1) Use Beta posterior with alpha=1,beta=1 prior for hit-rate uncertainty. 2) Gate TTL applies for prefixes with >=1000 samples in the last 7 days or confidence interval width <20 percentage points. 3) Deliver key-minimization suggestions as non-destructive recommendations (opt-in) for the first two quarters.
implementation_notes: Implemented a modular scoring function so we can swap the cost model (per-token vs per-request). The prototype lives behind a feature flag 'cache_thermostat_v1'. We instrumented new metrics: thermostat.suggested_ttl, thermostat.applied_ttl, thermostat.sim_delta_cost, thermostat.rollback_reason. Added tracing hooks for tracing a prefix "request-id -> prefix -> TTL-decision" end-to-end.
test_plan: Unit tests for TTL generator and key-simplifier logic. Integration tests run replay harness against staging KV cluster. Load test with synthetic high-cardinality prefixes to validate stability. A/B run comparing baseline vs thermostat on staging for 48 hours. Canary monitors automatically escalate to on-call if rollback triggers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: thermostats/overview, thermostats/rollout-health. Alerts: P95 latency increase >10% sustained for 10m; per-prefix hit-rate drop >20% for >5m; cost delta >10% sustained. Alerts post to #infra-thermostat and oncall rotation.
